items.title: Working at the frontier: How Cognition trusts Claude Fable 5 to work through the night | Claude by Anthropic
items.summary_1line: Cognition tested Claude Fable 5 in Devin, its AI software engineer. It's the first model its team trusts to run unattended for eight hours and deliver production-ready code.
items.editor_note: Cognition says Fable 5 is the first model it trusts to run unattended for eight hours in Devin.

items.title: Supporting ambitious external research through the Anthropic Economic Futures Research Fund
items.summary_1line: We’re committing $200 million to the Anthropic Economic Futures Research Fund to support ambitious external research.
items.editor_note: Anthropic commits $200M to the Economic Futures Research Fund for external research.

items.title: Think through hard problems in voice mode | Claude by Anthropic
items.summary_1line: Starting today, voice mode runs on Anthropic's Claude Opus, Claude Sonnet, and Claude Haiku, reaches the tools you’ve connected, and speaks many more languages.
items.editor_note: Voice mode expands to Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku with tool access and more languages.

editorial.tldr: This thread groups three unrelated Anthropic posts that happen to share the word "through": Cognition's trust in Claude Fable 5 for unattended coding, a $200M research-funding commitment, and a voice-mode expansion. There is no single connecting story here.
editorial.whats_new: The latest post: voice mode now runs on Claude Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku, reaches connected tools, and speaks more languages.
editorial.why_it_matters: None of the three items build on each other, so treat them as independent signals: production trust for autonomous coding agents, external R&D investment, and expanded voice/tool multimodality.
